newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas Advertising denies buy-out plan.
newsitem.headline: Havas Advertising denies buy-out plan.

text.p: Havas Advertising denied any possibility that it would be the object of either a leveraged or management buy-out.
"We formally deny any leveraged or management buy-out," a company spokesman told Reuters.

The sector has been anticipating a buy-out or some kind of ownership reshuffle since Compagnie Generale des Eaux and Havas Advertising parent Havas restructured their media activities earlier this month.

Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier said at the time that he envisaged reducing Havas's 37-percent holding in Havas Advertising, formed from the merger of Eurocom and RSCG, to 20 percent if the advertising unit entered an alliance to further its international development.
On Saturday Le Figaro newspaper said Pierre de Plas, former vice chairman of Eurocom, said he believed Havas had decided on a leveraged buy-out at its advertising subsidiary."

Friday's edition of Strategies, the advertising industry's weekly newspaper, suggested that Havas could float some shares in Havas Advertising if it wanted to cut its stake in the unit, or it could sell small percentages to institutional investors.

Finding a single buyer for the 17 percent which Dauzier said he would be prepared to part with would be hard, the weekly said, because at Havas Advertising's current share price that would be worth nearly 600 million francs.
An alliance with another advertising group does not seem likely, partly because of potential clashes between big clients the car sector, it said.

Havas Advertising shares surged on speculative buying on the Paris bourse on Monday but finally closed 23 francs down at 665 francs. Buying began again on Tuesday, with the share up 26 at 668 francs at 0946 GMT.
